mike-ops: We've got a weird 401 after rotating keys in Console. Staging still gets 401 invalid_api_key but a curl from my laptop with the new key succeeds. Anyone seen cached/old key behavior? trace: abc123

anna-support: Sorry to hear that — can you share the failing request (headers) from the service and how you rotated the key? Which cluster/cluster-region is this (staging-east etc.)?

mike-ops: Rotated via Console around 10:05. Service: staging-east. Failing request (redacted):

POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_OLDKEY...
User-Agent: my-service/1.2.3
Body: {"input":"hello"}

Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}

anna-support: Two quick checks: 1) confirm the process/release was restarted after rotation (some Node runtimes keep env in memory), 2) check for trailing/leading whitespace or stray quotes in the env value. You can print the raw bytes like:

```bash
printf '%s' "$REDWOOD_API_KEY" | xxd
```

mike-ops: Ran that on the failing host, results show a trailing 0a byte at the end. Oops.

sara-eng: That explains it — a newline becomes part of the header string and the server rejects it. Fix options: trim the var when exporting, or change app start script to strip whitespace. Example quick fix:

```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(echo -n "$REDWOOD_API_KEY")"
# or when loading from file:
REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(sed -e 's/[\r\n]*$//' /etc/secrets/redwood_key)
```

Also ensure you roll or restart all workers so no process keeps the old env.

mike-ops: Did the export + restarted the service, smoke curl now returns 200. Thanks!

anna-support: For the runbook, add a step after rotation: 1) restart all service instances, 2) validate env with xxd or printf, 3) run a quick curl smoke test: 

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Api-Key $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health || echo FAIL
```

mike-ops: Adding to runbook now. Appreciate the fast help :pray: :tada:

deploy-bot: Deployment staging-east/blue completed (rev 5f3)
